title: [WA-015] Integrate CEL expression engine and whitelisted functions
description:
# Goal

Integrate CEL for deterministic weather rule evaluation.

## Requirements

- Do not use Python `eval` or `exec`.
- Use a CEL implementation available for Python or isolate a CEL runtime if needed.
- Build a wrapper that:
  - validates syntax
  - validates allowed variables/functions
  - evaluates expressions against weather data
  - returns typed evaluation results
  - provides useful validation errors for the user

## Function allowlist exposed to the Foundation Model

The Foundation Model must receive this list in prompt/tool context when asked to propose CEL expressions.

### Time range helpers

- `now()`
- `today()`
- `tomorrow()`
- `weekend()`
- `next_hours(n)`
- `date_range(start_iso, end_iso)`
- `between(range, start_hhmm, end_hhmm)`
- `minutes(n)`
- `hours(n)`
- `previous_snapshot()`

### Aggregation/statistical helpers

- `min(metric, range)`
- `max(metric, range)`
- `avg(metric, range)`
- `sum(metric, range)`
- `median(metric, range)`
- `stddev(metric, range)`
- `pctl(metric, range, percentile)`

### Change/trend helpers

- `delta(metric, range)`
- `abs_delta(metric, range)`
- `rate_of_change(metric, range)`
- `forecast_delta(metric, range, previous_snapshot_ref)`

### Condition-over-time helpers

- `duration_where(condition, range)`
- `count_where(condition, range)`
- `any(condition, range)`
- `all(condition, range)`

### Numeric helpers

- `abs(x)`
- `round(x, digits)`
- `clamp(x, min_value, max_value)`

## Available metrics

At minimum:

- `temperature_2m_c`
- `apparent_temperature_c`
- `precipitation_mm`
- `precipitation_probability_pct`
- `rain_mm`
- `snowfall_cm`
- `cloud_cover_pct`
- `wind_speed_10m_ms`
- `wind_gusts_10m_ms`
- `wind_direction_10m_deg`
- `pressure_msl_hpa`
- `relative_humidity_2m_pct`
- `weather_code`

## Example expressions

```cel
max("wind_gusts_10m_ms", weekend()) >= 12
```

```cel
avg("wind_speed_10m_ms", next_hours(24)) >= 7
```

```cel
forecast_delta("apparent_temperature_c", tomorrow(), previous_snapshot()) <= -7
```

```cel
duration_where(precipitation_mm > 0.2, next_hours(12)) >= minutes(60)
```

## Acceptance criteria

- CEL syntax validation works before saving rules.
- Unknown function/metric names are rejected.
- Unit tests cover each helper category.
- The full function/metric list is available as a serializable object for prompts.
- Evaluator does not call the LLM.

description:
# Goal

Define the weather provider abstraction and normalized data contracts.

## Provider interfaces

Create three provider protocols/interfaces:

```python
class ForecastProvider(Protocol):
    async def get_forecast(
        self,
        location: LocationRef,
        time_range: TimeRange,
        variables: list[WeatherVariable],
        resolution: ForecastResolution,

```

```python
class ObservationProvider(Protocol):
    async def get_observations(
        self,
        location: LocationRef,
        radius_km: float,
        variables: list[WeatherVariable],
    ) -> ObservationResult: ...
```

```python
class WarningProvider(Protocol):
    async def get_warnings(
        self,
        location: LocationRef,
        time_range: TimeRange,
    ) -> list[WeatherWarning]: ...
```

## Required model types

Implement Pydantic/domain models:

```python
class LocationRef(BaseModel):
    id: str
    name: str
    latitude: float
    longitude: float
```

```python
class TimeRange(BaseModel):
    start: datetime
    end: datetime
    timezone: Literal["Europe/Warsaw"] = "Europe/Warsaw"
```

```python
class ForecastPoint(BaseModel):
    target_time: datetime
    fetched_at: datetime
    provider: str
    model: str | None
    location_id: str

    temperature_2m_c: float | None = None
    apparent_temperature_c: float | None = None
    precipitation_mm: float | None = None
    precipitation_probability_pct: float | None = None

    pressure_msl_hpa: float | None = None
    relative_humidity_2m_pct: float | None = None
    weather_code: str | None = None

    raw_payload: dict
```

```python
class ForecastResult(BaseModel):
    provider: str
    model: str | None
    location: LocationRef
    fetched_at: datetime
    points: list[ForecastPoint]
    raw_payload: dict
```

```python
class ObservationPoint(BaseModel):
    observed_at: datetime
    fetched_at: datetime
    provider: str
    station_id: str | None
```

- All normalized field names must include units where ambiguity exists.
- Preserve raw provider payloads.

title: [WA-008] Implement DateResolver for Polish natural time ranges
description:
# Goal

Implement deterministic resolution of Polish natural time ranges.

## Scope

Support:

- `dziś`
- `dziś wieczorem`
- `jutro`
- `jutro rano`
- `jutro po południu`
- `jutro wieczorem`
- `następne 3 dni`
- `weekend`
- `ten weekend`
- `następny weekend`
- `majówka`
- explicit date ranges

## Rules

Timezone is always `Europe/Warsaw`.

Suggested mappings:

- `dziś`: now to 23:59
- `dziś wieczorem`: today 18:00-23:00
- `jutro`: tomorrow 00:00-23:59
- `jutro rano`: tomorrow 06:00-10:00
- `jutro po południu`: tomorrow 12:00-18:00
- `jutro wieczorem`: tomorrow 18:00-23:00
- `następne 3 dni`: now to now + 72h
- `weekend`: nearest upcoming Saturday 00:00 to Sunday 23:59
- `majówka`: range around May 1 and May 3 for the relevant year, including adjacent weekend/bridge days if configured

## Holiday data

Use a public holiday provider abstraction. First implementation should use Nager.Date with local DB cache. The resolver must still work from cache when the API is temporarily unavailable.

## Acceptance criteria

- Deterministic unit tests with frozen clock.
- Tests cover edge cases around Friday/Saturday/Sunday.
- Tests cover "majówka" for at least two years.
- DateResolver returns explicit start/end datetimes and a human-readable explanation.

title: Telegram Weather AI Agent — LangGraph/LangSmith learning project
description:
# Epic: Telegram Weather AI Agent

Build a self-hosted Telegram weather AI agent for Polish-language usage.

## Product goal

The bot must:
- answer Polish natural-language weather questions,
- manage multiple named locations,
- create/edit/delete/snooze weather notification rules,
- evaluate scheduled and event-based notifications deterministically,
- send official IMGW alerts and current synoptic data,
- preserve conversation context per Telegram thread/topic,
- be deployed on a homelab via Docker Compose,
- use LangGraph/LangChain/LangSmith heavily as a learning objective.

## Key architecture decisions

- Telegram remains the user interface.
- Use Telegram private supergroup + Topics for threaded context.
- Context key: `chat_id + message_thread_id`; fallback to `chat_id`.
- Foundation model default: `gpt-5-mini`, configurable through LangChain.
- Supported language: Polish only.
- Supported timezone: `Europe/Warsaw` only for now.
- Units are global, not per location.
- Weather forecast source for MVP: Open-Meteo DWD ICON.
- Current observations: IMGW synop endpoint.
- Official warnings: IMGW meteorological/hydrological warnings.
- Holidays: public holiday API + local cache, preferably Nager.Date.
- Persistence: PostgreSQL + TimescaleDB.
- Rule expressions: CEL + whitelisted weather/statistical helper functions.
- LLM may propose raw CEL expressions, but user must confirm before activation.
- Anomalies are not special-cased; they are normal CEL-based rules.
- Rule evaluation must never depend on the LLM at runtime.
- Observability: LangSmith for LLM/LangGraph traces within free/low-cost limits; structured logs and DB audit for durable self-hosted observability.

## Global units

```yaml
temperature: celsius
wind_speed: m/s
precipitation: mm
pressure: hPa
```

## Definition of done for the Epic

The Epic is complete when:
- a user can run the system with `docker compose up`,
- the bot answers weather questions for named locations,
- the bot supports Telegram authorization,
- the bot supports location CRUD and global units,
- the bot resolves Polish natural time ranges like "jutro", "weekend", "majówka",
- the bot can create, edit, disable, delete, snooze, and explain rules,
- rules are evaluated via CEL using persisted weather snapshots,
- notifications contain short IDs for rules/events,
- Open-Meteo DWD ICON forecasts are fetched and persisted,
- IMGW warnings and synop observations are fetched and surfaced,
- LangGraph is used for the conversational workflow,
- LangSmith traces/evals are wired for learning,
- task-level tests and at least one end-to-end dry run pass.

title: Fix Telegram bot async lifecycle instead of running PTB in a worker thread
description:
## The Problem

In `src/weather_agent/cmd/bot.py`, the bot is started with `await asyncio.to_thread(bot.run)`. `bot.run()` calls `Application.run_polling()` in `src/weather_agent/adapters/telegram/bot.py`.

That is unsafe because `AppContainer` and HTTP clients are created on the main event loop, but `run_polling()` runs the Telegram application in a worker thread. It also changes PTB signal/shutdown behavior.

## Implementation Steps

1. Read `src/weather_agent/cmd/bot.py`.
2. Read `src/weather_agent/adapters/telegram/bot.py`, especially `TelegramBot.start()` and `TelegramBot.stop()`.
3. In `cmd_bot()`, replace `await asyncio.to_thread(bot.run)` with the async lifecycle.
4. After `bot.setup()`, call `await bot.start()`.
5. Keep the bot alive in the same event loop until cancelled. A simple loop is fine:
   `while True: await asyncio.sleep(3600)`
6. In a `finally` block, call `await bot.stop()`.
7. Do not remove the outer `asyncio.run(_run())`.
8. Keep pid file cleanup unchanged.

## Files To Modify

- `src/weather_agent/cmd/bot.py`

## Acceptance Criteria

- `cmd/bot.py` no longer contains `asyncio.to_thread(bot.run)`.
- Bot startup uses `await bot.start()`.
- Bot shutdown uses `await bot.stop()` in `finally`.
- `uv run ruff check src/weather_agent/cmd/bot.py` passes.
- `uv run mypy` passes.
- `uv run pytest tests/unit/test_main.py -x -v -k bot` passes.

title: Fix multi-time schedule_notification crash from parallel tool calls
description:
Diagnosed regression from LangSmith trace root 019ddd76-9a95-7201-bec2-2dabf212b381 in project weather-agent-dev. User asked in Polish: "wyślij mi jeszcze raz taką prognozę dziś o 14 i o 18" after an RC plane forecast for Gdynia. The model behavior was semantically correct: DeepAgents/LangGraph emitted two schedule_notification tool calls, for 2026-04-30T14:00:00+02:00 and 2026-04-30T18:00:00+02:00. Failure was sqlalchemy.exc.InvalidRequestError: Session is already flushing.

Root cause: LangGraph/DeepAgents executes parallel tool calls with asyncio.gather. Both schedule_notification calls share the same RulesToolbox -> ThreadMemoryService -> TelegramContextService -> AsyncSession created in src/weather_agent/adapters/telegram/handler.py. Concurrent flush on one AsyncSession crashes.

Files to inspect: src/weather_agent/adapters/telegram/handler.py, rules tool/toolbox code that implements schedule_notification, ThreadMemoryService, TelegramContextService, repository/session factory wiring, and tests around Telegram scheduling/pending confirmations.

Implementation guidance: prevent concurrent use of a single AsyncSession by parallel tool calls. Keep the fix narrow and urgent; do not wait for the whole DI/lifecycle epic if that would delay the crash fix. Preserve Polish user-facing behavior.
design: Smallest safe approach: prefer moving DB-writing tool operations behind a per-tool-call session boundary or short-lived session factory, aligned with future AppContainer/DI work. If introducing full DI is too large, add a narrow session-factory boundary only for RulesToolbox/ThreadMemoryService writes. Do not reuse one AsyncSession across parallel tool calls. Related context: weather-agent-xms Epic 1 DI/lifecycle, weather-agent-xms.2 replace BotServices/lazy service access, weather-agent-k2u.3 ThreadMemoryService metadata scope.
acceptance_criteria:
- A request with two times like "dziś o 14 i o 18" does not crash when DeepAgents emits multiple schedule_notification tool calls.
- No shared AsyncSession is used concurrently by parallel tool calls.
- User-facing responses remain Polish.
- Existing single schedule flow still works.
- Tests cover the regression.
notes: Do not mark this as blocked by weather-agent-xms.2 unless implementation genuinely requires the full AppContainer migration. Prefer a local session-factory seam for the urgent bug. Product follow-up for multiple confirmations is tracked separately because fixing AsyncSession concurrency alone does not make multi-time scheduling UX correct.

title: Use home/default fallback in weather location resolution flow
description:
## Goal
Update weather location resolution so a weather query like `jaka pogoda za dwa dni?` can use the persisted home/default location when the extractor returns no explicit location.

## Step-by-step guidance
1. Inspect `resolve_location_node` in `src/weather_agent/graphs/nodes/weather_qa.py` around lines 650-699.
2. Preserve existing successful behaviors for explicit extracted location, existing `state.resolved_location`, and reply context turns.
3. Add a deterministic persisted home/default lookup after existing state/reply-context checks and before producing a missing-location error.
4. Use the LocationService API from the sibling task; do not query storage directly from the graph if a service abstraction exists.
5. Ensure the lookup uses the correct conversation/context identity. For Telegram, preserve topic-aware context using `chat_id + message_thread_id` and fallback to `chat_id`.
6. Keep MVP responses Polish-only and timezone handling at `Europe/Warsaw` unless existing code already supplies a different configured value.
7. Do not ask the LLM to infer the missing location from memory.
8. Add unit tests in `tests/unit/graphs/test_weather_qa.py` or the closest existing file for precedence and missing-location behavior.
9. Add an integration/e2e-style regression test covering: saved home location, user asks `jaka pogoda za dwa dni?`, resolved location is the saved home/default and the flow does not produce generic retry.

## Required precedence
1. Explicit extracted location from the current user message.
2. Existing `state.resolved_location` and/or reply context location when appropriate.
3. Persisted home/default location for the conversation context.
4. Specific missing-location error/prompt if none of the above exist.
design: This is a graph orchestration change, not prompt tuning. The fallback should be a pure deterministic service call. Keep provider contracts unchanged and only pass a resolved location forward once it has been selected by the documented precedence.
acceptance_criteria:
- Weather resolution uses persisted home/default location when the current query has no explicit location.
- Explicit message location still overrides any saved home/default location.
- Existing state or reply-context location behavior is preserved and tested.

title: Fix remembered home location fallback for weather queries
description:
## Problem
A user can receive a successful Polish confirmation that the bot remembered a home location, but a later weather query without an explicit location fails with a generic retry error instead of using the remembered location or asking specifically for a location.

## User reproduction
1. User sets home location and receives: `Zapamiętałem Twoją lokalizację domową jako Rogalińska 11, Gdańsk. W czym mogę pomóc z pogodą?`
2. User asks: `jaka pogoda za dwa dni?`
3. Bot replies: `Przepraszam, wystąpił błąd. Spróbuj ponownie za chwilę.`

## Trace evidence
The LangSmith trace for the failed weather question shows the location extractor behaved correctly for `jaka pogoda za dwa dni?`:
- returned `_LocationExtraction(location_name=None, focus=None)`
- metadata includes `context_key="7431473393"`, `is_reply_follow_up=false`, `node="handle_weather"`
This means the weather flow must deterministically recover a persisted default/home location or return a specific missing-location prompt; it must not rely on LLM memory.

## Code findings to verify during implementation
- `resolve_location_node` in `src/weather_agent/graphs/nodes/weather_qa.py` around lines 650-699 only uses explicit extracted location, existing `state.resolved_location`, or `reply_context_turns`; it does not load any persisted home/default location.
- `weather_agent_node` in `src/weather_agent/graphs/nodes/weather_qa.py` around lines 507-512 turns any `state.error` into generic `_GENERIC_USER_ERROR`.
- `ConversationOrchestrator._handle_weather` in `src/weather_agent/graphs/conversation.py` around lines 430-466 continues into `weather_agent_node` even when `resolve_location_node` returned an error, which can mask a specific missing-location error.
- `README.md` around lines 188-192 mentions `/dodaj_lok`, but `src/weather_agent/adapters/telegram/bot.py` around lines 44-47 wires only `/start`, `/help`, and `/status`. Verify the persistence path that produced the `Zapamiętałem...` message before assuming it exists.
- `LocationService` in `src/weather_agent/domain/locations.py` currently supports create/list/resolve by query, but has no explicit default/home lookup.

## Architecture constraints
- Preserve Telegram topic-aware context: key by `chat_id + message_thread_id`, with `chat_id` fallback.
- MVP remains Polish-only and defaults to `Europe/Warsaw`.
- Runtime weather/rule logic must be deterministic and must not rely on LLM memory.
- Preserve provider split between forecast, observation, and warning contracts.

## Desired behavior
For a weather query with no explicit location, the bot should resolve location using deterministic precedence: explicit extracted location, current state or reply context, persisted home/default location for the conversation context, then a specific Polish missing-location prompt if no fallback exists. Generic retry should be reserved for unexpected failures, not normal missing-location conditions.
design: Implement as a small deterministic location-resolution repair, not as prompt tuning. First verify how the `Zapamiętałem...` message is produced and whether it persists data. Then add or expose a domain-level home/default lookup in `LocationService`. Finally use that lookup in `resolve_location_node` before emitting missing-location errors, and preserve specific resolution errors in `ConversationOrchestrator._handle_weather`.
acceptance_criteria:
- Reproduction no longer returns the generic retry message after a valid home location has been persisted.
- Weather queries without explicit location use a deterministic persisted home/default fallback when available for the Telegram context key, including chat/thread handling with chat fallback.
- If no location can be resolved, the user receives a specific Polish missing-location prompt rather than `Przepraszam, wystąpił błąd. Spróbuj ponownie za chwilę.`
- The implementation is covered by unit and integration/regression tests for location persistence, location resolution precedence, and error preservation.
- No runtime fallback depends on LLM memory or non-deterministic inference.
notes: This parent tracks the complete home-location fallback bug. Child tasks are intentionally detailed for a less capable implementation agent; work through them in order and do not close this parent until all children are implemented and quality gates pass.
close_reason: All 5 child tasks implemented and verified: /dodaj_lok command wired with persistence, LocationService.get_default_location() added, home/default fallback integrated into resolve_location_node, missing-location errors preserved instead of masked. 1085/1086 tests pass (1 flaky pre-existing PID lock test). Ruff clean. Mypy no new errors.

title: Eliminate redundant LLM calls in weather flow (7 calls → 1-2)
description:
The weather handler makes 7 LLM calls per turn (84s, ~/usr/bin/zsh.008/request) when 1-2 would suffice:

1. _extract_location_and_focus called TWICE: once in resolve_location_node, again in weather_agent_node (same user message)
2. Geocoder._ask_llm called 2-3 times for same location ('Gdynia'): once per resolve_location in each forecast tool call  
3. After each forecast tool result, _resolve_location called AGAIN (line 610-624) just to update state
4. Agent makes 2 forecast calls because first time_expression resolves to only today

Fixes:
- Skip _extract_location_and_focus in weather_agent_node when location/focus already in state
- Geocoder: try direct geocode API first, LLM fallback only on failure
- Remove post-forecast _resolve_location (use already-resolved location from state)
- Pass pre-resolved location into tool calls so agent tools don't re-geocode
close_reason: Implemented 4 fixes: (1) skip duplicate _extract_location_and_focus in weather_agent_node by using state's resolved_location+user_focus instead of 2nd LLM call; (2) Geocoder.geocode tries direct API first, LLM fallback only on direct failure (saves ~3.5s per call for simple names); (3) removed post-forecast _resolve_location call (lines 610-624) that was re-resolving already-known locations; (4) passed pre-resolved location through _execute_tool_call → _execute_get_forecast/_execute_get_observations so agent tools skip geocoding entirely when location already in state. All 1072 tests pass.

title: Deep Grafana Cloud observability for app and Postgres
description:
Goal:
Add deep operational observability for this project using Grafana Cloud for logs and metrics, while keeping LangSmith for conversational/model traces.

Scope decisions already made:
- Grafana Cloud scope is limited to application services and Postgres.
- Do not add host-level or container-level exporters such as node-exporter or cAdvisor in this workstream.
- Logs may include sanitized conversation metadata, but should avoid raw user message bodies by default.
- LangSmith remains in place for traces; this epic is about logs and metrics, not replacing LangSmith.

Why this work is needed:
- src/weather_agent/observability/logging.py already defines structured JSON logging helpers and audit logging, but most runtime modules still use plain logging.getLogger(__name__) and printf-style logs.
- docker-compose.yml currently writes container logs with the Docker json-file driver, but nothing ships those logs to Grafana Cloud Loki.
- pyproject.toml currently has no Prometheus metrics dependency and the runtime exposes no /metrics endpoint.
- src/weather_agent/api/health.py exists, but it is not currently started by the bot or worker runtime and it exposes only /health, not Prometheus metrics.
- The project needs operational visibility for exceptions, provider/API issues, worker failures, Telegram send failures, and rule-evaluation behavior. LangSmith alone is not enough for those concerns.

Desired end state:
- Bot and worker emit consistent structured JSON logs to stdout/stderr.
- Grafana Alloy collects those logs and ships them to Grafana Cloud Loki.
- Bot and worker expose Prometheus metrics endpoints.
- Grafana Alloy scrapes app metrics and Postgres exporter metrics and remote-writes them to Grafana Cloud Prometheus.
- Observability data is privacy-conscious: no secrets, no raw conversation payloads by default, no high-cardinality metric labels.
- Operators can use Grafana Cloud dashboards/queries to answer operational questions such as:
  - Are Telegram messages being processed?
  - Are provider/API failures spiking?
  - Is the worker still evaluating rules on schedule?
  - Are notifications being sent or failing?
  - Is Postgres healthy from the application's perspective?

This observability workstream should complement, not conflict with, the LangSmith tasks already created under weather-agent-eot.8 through weather-agent-eot.11.
design:
Recommended implementation order:
1. Standardize app logging and contextual log fields.
2. Expose observability HTTP surfaces (/health and /metrics) for bot and worker.
3. Add application/business metrics for key bot and worker flows.
4. Add Grafana Alloy plus Postgres exporter and wire Docker Compose to Grafana Cloud.
5. Add verification, operator docs, dashboard/query guidance, and alert guidance.

Constraints:
- Keep logs on stdout/stderr; do not push logs directly from Python to Loki.
- Prefer Grafana Alloy as the collection plane.
- Keep metric labels low-cardinality.
- Keep trace/log/metric correlation possible via correlation_id and related metadata.
acceptance_criteria:
This epic is complete when:
- The bot and worker emit structured application logs suitable for Loki.
- The bot and worker expose Prometheus metrics and those metrics include key operational and business signals.
- Docker Compose includes Grafana Alloy and Postgres exporter configured for Grafana Cloud ingestion.
- Documentation and verification steps exist so a follow-up operator can confirm that logs and metrics are really arriving in Grafana Cloud.

title: Make LangSmith configuration, disable semantics, and status surfaces authoritative
description:
Problem statement:
The current LangSmith integration reports a simple enabled/disabled state, but that state is not authoritative and can be misleading.

Current behavior from review:
- src/weather_agent/observability/langsmith_tracing.py configure_tracing() only manipulates LANGCHAIN_* environment variables.
- The installed langsmith client also supports LANGSMITH_* environment variables and context-based tracing state.
- LangSmithTracing.is_enabled() only checks whether LANGCHAIN_TRACING_V2 == 'true'.
- src/weather_agent/api/health.py and src/weather_agent/adapters/telegram/commands.py use LangSmithTracing.is_enabled() for /health and /status.
- If tracing is enabled with no API key, or with external LANGSMITH_* env vars, status can say 'enabled' while uploads may fail or disabling may be incomplete.
- configure_tracing(enabled=False) clears LANGCHAIN_* vars but does not explicitly account for LANGSMITH_* vars that may still affect the client.

Goal:
- Make tracing configuration and status truthful.
- Handle both LANGSMITH_* and LANGCHAIN_* semantics deliberately.
- Ensure disable behavior is well-defined and status/health surfaces reflect the actual tracing state the runtime will use.

Implementation guidance for the follow-up agent:
- Prefer using the LangSmith library's own tracing-state helpers where possible instead of a hand-rolled env check.
- Decide and document what /status and /health should mean:
  - configured
  - enabled
  - upload-capable
  - or some combination
- If the app owns tracing config, make disable semantics explicit for both namespaces.
- If external env vars should override app config, document that and reflect it in status.
- Important file touchpoints:
  - src/weather_agent/observability/langsmith_tracing.py
  - src/weather_agent/api/health.py
  - src/weather_agent/adapters/telegram/commands.py
  - src/weather_agent/settings.py
  - tests/unit/observability/test_langsmith_tracing.py
  - tests/unit/api/test_health.py
- Consider whether it is better for health/status to expose more than one field instead of a single boolean if that improves truthfulness.

Constraints:
- Keep LangSmith optional for correctness.
- Do not break startup when tracing is disabled or partially configured.
design:
Recommended design shape:
- One source of truth for tracing state.
- Explicit distinction between 'tracing logically enabled' and 'likely able to upload to LangSmith'.
- Avoid status surfaces that simply mirror one env var and mislead operators.
- Keep configuration behavior compatible with local development and external env overrides.
acceptance_criteria:
This issue is complete when all of the following are true:
- The runtime has a clear and documented source of truth for LangSmith tracing state.
- /health and /status no longer rely on a misleading LANGCHAIN_TRACING_V2-only boolean.
- Disable semantics are deliberate and tested for both LANGCHAIN_* and LANGSMITH_* style configuration.
- Tests cover enabled, disabled, externally-overridden, and missing-api-key scenarios.
notes:
Key nuance:
- A boolean called 'langsmith_enabled' is too easy to misinterpret. The follow-up agent should consider whether the status model needs separate 'configured', 'enabled', and/or 'upload_ready' concepts.
close_reason: Implemented: authoritative LangSmith config with both LANGCHAIN/LANGSMITH namespace handling, get_status() rich status, and conversational runtime tracing with trace() on graph nodes and @traceable on weather tool execution. All tests, ruff, mypy pass.

title: Instrument LangSmith traces for conversational runtime and tool execution
description:
Problem statement:
The repo currently enables LangSmith mostly by setting environment variables early in startup, but the main conversational runtime is not instrumented deeply enough to provide the graph/tool visibility the project expects.

Current behavior from review:
- src/weather_agent/__main__.py calls configure_tracing(settings.langsmith) before services are initialized, which is a good start.
- src/weather_agent/graphs/nodes/weather_qa.py uses a LangChain chat model, so model calls may be traced.
- However, tool execution is handled manually through _build_tools() JSON schemas plus _execute_tool_call(), _execute_get_forecast(), and _execute_get_observations() rather than traceable LangChain tools or LangSmith-decorated functions.
- The repo docs/specs expect graph path and tool calls to be visible in LangSmith, but the current code likely only shows model spans and not the real tool execution tree.
- There is no explicit tracing metadata around inbound Telegram turns, graph invocation, reply-based context, or final answer send.

Goal:
- Produce a rich, nested LangSmith trace tree for the conversational bot path.
- A single Telegram message should be traceable across major steps such as:
  - inbound message handling
  - graph invocation
  - intent routing
  - reply-context loading
  - location/time resolution
  - LLM answer generation
  - get_forecast / get_observations tool execution
  - geocoder/date/provider calls
  - final reply send
- Preserve natural-language UX and deterministic provider behavior.

Implementation guidance for the follow-up agent:
- Investigate whether LangGraph can be invoked with explicit run config / metadata from src/weather_agent/__main__.py so each Telegram turn has a stable run name, tags, and metadata.
- Add manual LangSmith instrumentation to custom runtime boundaries that are not automatically traced by LangChain.
- Likely options:
  - wrap critical functions with langsmith traceable decorators or equivalent context managers, or
  - replace manual tool-dispatch surfaces with actual LangChain/StructuredTool surfaces where that materially improves trace visibility without making the design worse.
- Important file touchpoints:
  - src/weather_agent/__main__.py
  - src/weather_agent/graphs/conversation.py
  - src/weather_agent/graphs/nodes/weather_qa.py
  - src/weather_agent/graphs/nodes/rule_management.py
  - src/weather_agent/infrastructure/geocoder.py
  - src/weather_agent/domain/date_resolver.py if tracing is added there
  - any answer-send boundary where the final Telegram reply is emitted
- Suggested trace metadata/tags to consider:
  - context_key
  - chat_id
  - message_thread_id
  - telegram_user_id
  - inbound message_id
  - reply_to_message_id
  - resolved_intent
  - model provider / model name
  - whether the message was a reply follow-up
- Be careful not to stuff large raw provider payloads into LangSmith metadata. Prefer concise metadata and normal return values over huge blobs.
- Be careful not to log secrets such as bot token or model API key into LangSmith metadata.

Constraints:
- This task is about tracing, not changing product behavior.
- Runtime correctness must remain deterministic outside the LLM.
- The bot must remain Polish-only and natural-language-first.
design:
Recommended design shape:
- Keep LangSmith as observability, not correctness.
- Prefer explicit spans around custom code paths rather than assuming env-level auto-instrumentation is enough.
- Model one top-level span per inbound Telegram turn.
- Make tool calls visible either as real tools or explicit tool-type spans.
- Preserve readable trace hierarchy: message handler -> graph -> node/tool spans -> provider/geocoder spans.
acceptance_criteria:
This issue is complete when all of the following are true:
- A natural-language weather question produces a LangSmith trace tree with at least the Telegram turn, graph invocation, model call, and concrete weather tool execution visible.
- A reply-based follow-up question also produces a trace that clearly indicates reply-context loading and follow-up handling.
- Tool execution is no longer a black box hidden behind custom Python dispatch with no LangSmith visibility.
- No secrets are written into trace metadata.
- Tests or reproducible verification steps confirm the trace hierarchy for at least one conversational weather flow.
notes:
Useful reproducible scenario for verification:
1. User asks: 'Czy brac dzisiaj parasol?'
2. Bot resolves weather context and answers.
3. User replies to that bot answer: 'A jutro?'
Expected trace coverage: two linked conversational turns, tool/provider visibility, and explicit reply-context handling on the second turn.

Relevant docs/spec context:
- docs/adr/0002-langgraph-learning-stack.md expects LangSmith to support learning/diagnostics.
- docs/specs/implement-epic-20260428T103903Z-c27038d9.md says LangGraph traces and LangSmith instrumentation should expose graph path and tool calls.
close_reason: Implemented: authoritative LangSmith config with both LANGCHAIN/LANGSMITH namespace handling, get_status() rich status, and conversational runtime tracing with trace() on graph nodes and @traceable on weather tool execution. All tests, ruff, mypy pass.

title: Fix previous snapshot selection for forecast_delta rule evaluation
description:
Problem statement:
forecast_delta-style rule evaluation is very likely comparing the wrong forecast data because forecast points are loaded without snapshot scoping.

Current behavior from code review:
- src/weather_agent/infrastructure/worker/rule_evaluator.py _build_evaluation_data() fetches the latest snapshot object for a location.
- It then loads current points via ForecastRepository.get_points_by_time_range(location_id, start, end).
- src/weather_agent/infrastructure/repositories/forecast_repository.py get_points_by_time_range() filters only by location_id and target_time, not by snapshot_id.
- If the database contains multiple forecast snapshots for the same location and overlapping target times, the current point set can mix rows from multiple snapshots.
- _build_evaluation_data() also fetches a previous snapshot object, but then loads previous_points with the same unfiltered time-range query, so previous data can duplicate or mix current data.

Target behavior:
- Current evaluation points must come only from the current snapshot being evaluated.
- Previous evaluation points must come only from the previous snapshot selected by get_previous_snapshot().
- forecast_delta and related comparisons must operate on truly distinct snapshots.

Implementation guidance for the follow-up agent:
- Add a snapshot-scoped repository query such as get_points_for_snapshot(snapshot_id, start, end) or equivalent.
- Update _build_evaluation_data() to load both current and previous point sets with explicit snapshot scoping.
- Re-check whether any other rule-evaluation helpers assume mixed point sets today.
- Likely touchpoints:
  - src/weather_agent/infrastructure/worker/rule_evaluator.py
  - src/weather_agent/infrastructure/repositories/forecast_repository.py
  - tests/unit/infrastructure/worker/test_rule_evaluator.py
  - tests/unit/infrastructure/test_repositories.py
design:
Recommended design shape:
- Keep snapshot selection deterministic and explicit.
- Make the repository API clearly express whether a query is location-scoped or snapshot-scoped.
- Do not rely on ordering or timing heuristics to infer which snapshot a point belongs to; use snapshot_id directly.
acceptance_criteria:
This issue is complete when all of the following are true:
- Current and previous forecast point collections are each loaded from exactly one snapshot.
- A regression test creates at least two snapshots for the same location with overlapping target times but different metric values, and forecast_delta uses the actual previous snapshot values.
- There is no mixed-snapshot point set in the evaluation data for either current or previous points.
notes:
Important nuance:
- This is not only a previous_points bug. The current points query is also suspicious because it ignores snapshot_id and can mix multiple stored snapshots for the same location/time window.
close_reason: Implemented and verified with tests, ruff, mypy

title: Make geocoding deterministic and stop trusting LLM-provided coordinates
description:
Problem statement:
The current geocoder can trust coordinates invented by the LLM, which is a correctness risk for a weather bot.

Current behavior from code review:
- src/weather_agent/infrastructure/geocoder.py geocode() calls _ask_llm() when a model_factory is present.
- If the model returns lat/lon, geocode() immediately returns a LocationRef with id formatted like 'llm:<lat>:<lon>'.
- That means the forecast path can operate on coordinates that never came from a deterministic geocoder or a saved user location.

Target behavior:
- Final coordinates used for forecast/rule logic should come from deterministic sources only:
  - a saved user location, or
  - the external geocoding API / deterministic geocoder adapter.
- Natural-language interpretation and disambiguation can still be conversational.
- The bot should still handle inflected Polish names and ambiguous locations gracefully.

Implementation guidance for the follow-up agent:
- Remove or neutralize the path that treats raw LLM lat/lon as authoritative coordinates.
- The LLM may still help normalize user phrasing into a safer search query, but the final coordinates should be resolved by deterministic geocoding or an existing stored location.
- Consider how to handle ambiguous names conversationally instead of silently accepting a guessed coordinate.
- Likely touchpoints:
  - src/weather_agent/infrastructure/geocoder.py
  - src/weather_agent/domain/locations.py
  - tests/unit/adapters/open_meteo/test_forecast_provider.py if location assumptions surface there
  - tests/unit/domain/test_locations.py
  - any geocoder-specific tests that should be added
design:
Recommended design shape:
- Keep the LLM in an assistive role only for language normalization or disambiguation prompts.
- Keep coordinate trust in deterministic adapters.
- Preserve the conversational UX by asking the user clarifying follow-up questions when a place name is ambiguous or under-specified.
- Prefer stable location identifiers from saved locations or geocoding API results rather than synthetic 'llm:' identifiers.
acceptance_criteria:
This issue is complete when all of the following are true:
- The bot no longer uses model-invented coordinates directly as forecast/rule inputs.
- A place mention can still be normalized from natural Polish phrasing such as 'w Gdansku' or a place nickname, but final coordinates come from deterministic resolution.
- Ambiguous place names are handled conversationally rather than by silently trusting an LLM guess.
- Tests demonstrate that untrusted model lat/lon are ignored or validated through a deterministic source before use.
notes:
Key constraint:
- This task must not remove conversational location handling. It should move coordinate trust, not make the bot less natural to use.
close_reason: Implemented and verified with tests, ruff, mypy

title: Fix persisted pending confirmation and multi-turn rule flow
description:
Problem statement:
The rule-confirmation flow is currently modeled as if proposing a rule, asking for confirmation, and persisting the rule can all happen inside one graph invocation. That does not match the intended multi-turn Telegram UX.

Current behavior from code review:
- src/weather_agent/graphs/conversation.py chains propose_cel_rule -> require_user_confirmation -> persist_rule_change in one run.
- src/weather_agent/graphs/nodes/rule_management.py require_user_confirmation_node() only asks the user 'Czy chcesz potwierdzic? (tak/nie)'.
- src/weather_agent/graphs/nodes/rule_management.py persist_rule_change_node() expects the current state.user_message itself to be the confirmation text such as 'tak' or 'nie'.
- src/weather_agent/infrastructure/memory/thread_memory.py already has methods for persisting pending_confirmation, but the active graph/runtime does not wire them in.

Target behavior:
- When the bot proposes a rule, it should persist pending confirmation and stop.
- The rule must not be created or edited until a later user turn explicitly confirms it.
- Confirmation should work whether the user sends a plain 'tak/nie' in the same thread context or replies directly to the bot's confirmation prompt.
- Pending confirmation should clear after explicit confirm/cancel or after expiry.

Implementation guidance for the follow-up agent:
- Persist pending_confirmation via ThreadMemoryService or equivalent persistent context layer after the proposal turn.
- Load pending_confirmation into ConversationState at the start of later turns.
- Route confirmation/cancellation as a distinct multi-turn path instead of asking and consuming confirmation in the same graph pass.
- Make reply-based confirmation first-class: if the user replies 'tak' to the confirmation prompt, that should resolve against the correct pending proposal for that context.
- Keep rule creation deterministic; only proposal generation may involve the LLM.
- Likely touchpoints:
  - src/weather_agent/graphs/conversation.py
  - src/weather_agent/graphs/state.py
  - src/weather_agent/graphs/nodes/rule_management.py
  - src/weather_agent/infrastructure/memory/thread_memory.py
  - src/weather_agent/adapters/telegram/context.py
  - tests/unit/graphs/test_rule_management.py
  - tests/e2e/test_mvp_workflow.py
design:
Recommended design shape:
- Separate 'proposal turn' from 'confirmation turn'.
- Persist only the minimum deterministic payload needed to later apply the change:
  - action (create_rule or edit_rule)
  - cel_expression
  - explanation
  - edit_short_id if editing
  - resolved location identifier
  - timestamps / expiry metadata
- Prefer explicit clear/load/store behavior in one place rather than spreading pending_confirmation mutations across multiple nodes.
- If LangGraph is kept, its node boundaries should match true user turns.
acceptance_criteria:
This issue is complete when all of the following are true:
- A natural-language rule request causes the bot to propose a rule and persist pending confirmation, but does not create the rule yet.
- A later user message 'tak' creates or edits the rule.
- A later user message 'nie' cancels the pending operation and clears it.
- Replying 'tak' directly to the bot's confirmation prompt also works.
- Unrelated follow-up weather questions do not accidentally create the pending rule.
- Tests cover confirm, cancel, expiry, and reply-based confirmation behavior.
notes:
Known implementation trap:
- The current graph shape encourages same-turn confirmation semantics even though Telegram confirmation is inherently a later-turn interaction.

Suggested regression example:
1. User: 'Powiadom mnie, jesli w weekend porywy wiatru beda powyzej 12 m/s.'
2. Bot: proposes CEL and asks for confirmation.
3. User: replies 'tak'.
4. Rule is created exactly once.
close_reason: Implemented and verified with tests, ruff, mypy

title: Support reply-based follow-up context and persisted turn memory
description:
Problem statement:
The current runtime does not support reply-based conversational follow-ups in the required way.

Current behavior from code review:
- src/weather_agent/__main__.py builds a fresh ConversationState per inbound Telegram message with only authorized_user_id, chat_id, message_thread_id, context_key, and user_message.
- src/weather_agent/__main__.py does not pass reply metadata such as message_id or reply_to_message.message_id into the state.
- src/weather_agent/graphs/conversation.py load_thread_context() only returns context_key.
- src/weather_agent/graphs/conversation.py save_thread_context() is a no-op.
- src/weather_agent/infrastructure/memory/thread_memory.py already has persistent storage for pending_confirmation and recent_context keyed by context_key.
- src/weather_agent/adapters/telegram/context.py already has TelegramContextService for persisted metadata.

Target behavior:
- If the user replies to a previous bot message, that replied-to bot turn becomes the primary context anchor for the next answer.
- The bot should also use a small recent thread context window so follow-ups remain natural without requiring the user to restate the location/time/focus every turn.
- Context must remain scoped by chat_id + message_thread_id, with chat_id fallback.
- The solution must keep the bot conversational and natural-language-first.

Implementation guidance for the follow-up agent:
- Extend the runtime state to include inbound Telegram metadata that matters for follow-ups:
  - inbound message_id
  - reply_to_message_id
  - reply_to_message_text if available
  - possibly a loaded reply anchor / recent context payload
- Persist compact turn records for both user and bot messages. Suggested turn fields:
  - message_id
  - role (user or bot)
  - text
  - answer_summary for bot turns
  - resolved_location
  - resolved_time_range
  - user_focus
  - timestamp
- Do not store unbounded raw transcripts. Keep a compact bounded history or compact summaries in TelegramContext metadata.
- Retrieval order should be explicit:
  1. replied-to message context, if the new Telegram message is a reply
  2. recent context window for the same context_key
  3. current user message
- The implementer will likely need to capture the outbound Telegram message returned by update.message.reply_text(answer) so the bot's message_id can be persisted and later matched by reply_to_message.message_id.
- Likely touchpoints:
  - src/weather_agent/__main__.py
  - src/weather_agent/graphs/state.py
  - src/weather_agent/graphs/conversation.py
  - src/weather_agent/infrastructure/memory/thread_memory.py
  - src/weather_agent/adapters/telegram/context.py
  - tests/unit/infrastructure/test_thread_memory.py
  - tests/unit/graphs/*
  - tests/e2e/test_mvp_workflow.py

The follow-up agent should preserve Polish responses and Europe/Warsaw assumptions.
design:
Recommended design shape:
- Keep context persistence deterministic and outside the LLM.
- Use TelegramContext metadata as the persistence boundary, not in-memory objects only.
- Model reply-based follow-up as a first-class retrieval step, not as a best-effort prompt hack.
- Prefer storing a compact per-turn record keyed by Telegram message_id so exact reply anchoring is possible.
- Use recent context to fill gaps such as implicit location/time/focus, but prioritize the explicit reply anchor when present.
- Avoid storing large full-answer payloads when a concise summary is enough for follow-up reasoning.
acceptance_criteria:
This issue is complete when all of the following are true:
- A user can ask a natural-language weather question, get a bot answer, reply to that specific bot message with 'A jutro?', and receive an answer that uses the prior answer as context.
- A user can reply 'A w Chwarznie?' to a previous answer and the bot understands that only the location changed.
- A user can reply 'A czy na rower bedzie za zimno?' to a previous forecast answer and the bot reuses the existing time/location context.
- Context remains isolated by chat_id + message_thread_id, with chat_id fallback when no topic exists.
- Persisted turn memory is bounded and deterministic.
- Tests cover reply-based anchor lookup, recent-context fallback, and thread/topic isolation.
notes:
Known implementation trap:
- Without persisting the bot's outbound message_id, Telegram reply_to_message.message_id cannot be mapped back to the specific prior bot turn.

Suggested verification ideas:
- Unit-test load/save of turn records.
- Graph/runtime test where the second user message is a reply to the first bot answer.
- E2E flow for 'Czy brac dzisiaj parasol?' followed by reply 'A jutro?'.

title: Conversational reliability and simplification for Telegram weather bot MVP
description:
Goal: keep the Telegram bot natural-language-first and conversational while making the runtime reliable enough for real follow-up questions.

Hard product requirements:
- If a user replies to a previous bot message in Telegram, the bot must use that replied-to message as context for the new answer.
- Preserve topic-aware scoping via chat_id + message_thread_id, with chat_id fallback when no topic/thread exists.
- Keep the MVP Polish-only and default to Europe/Warsaw.
- Keep runtime rule evaluation deterministic; it must never call the LLM.
- Preserve the provider split between forecast, observation, and warning contracts.
- Do not simplify the UX into slash-command-only flows. Slash commands can exist, but natural-language conversation remains the primary experience.

Current review findings that drive this epic:
- src/weather_agent/graphs/conversation.py has stubbed context hooks: load_thread_context() only returns context_key, and save_thread_context() is a no-op.
- src/weather_agent/__main__.py builds a fresh ConversationState for each message and does not pass reply-to metadata from Telegram.
- src/weather_agent/graphs/conversation.py currently chains propose_cel_rule -> require_user_confirmation -> persist_rule_change in one invocation, which does not match the desired multi-turn confirmation UX.
- src/weather_agent/infrastructure/memory/thread_memory.py and src/weather_agent/adapters/telegram/context.py already provide persistent storage primitives, but they are not wired into the active runtime.
- src/weather_agent/infrastructure/worker/rule_evaluator.py likely mixes or mis-selects forecast snapshots when evaluating forecast_delta-style rules.
- src/weather_agent/infrastructure/geocoder.py currently trusts LLM-produced coordinates directly.

title: Handle invalid persisted PendingConfirmation data safely after Pydantic migration
description:
## The Problem

`PendingConfirmation` is now a Pydantic model. `PendingConfirmation.from_dict()` can raise a validation error if old or malformed metadata exists in the database.

Some callers parse persisted metadata without handling validation errors:

- `src/weather_agent/adapters/telegram/handler.py` around `new_pending = await memory_service.get_pending_confirmation(...)`
- `src/weather_agent/llm/tools/rules_tools.py` in `_execute_confirm()`
- `src/weather_agent/llm/tools/rules_tools.py` in `_execute_cancel()`

A bad pending confirmation should not crash message handling or tool execution.

## Implementation Steps

1. Read `src/weather_agent/application/conversation_models.py`.
2. Read `src/weather_agent/adapters/telegram/handler.py` around pending confirmation parsing.
3. Read `src/weather_agent/llm/tools/rules_tools.py` around `_execute_confirm()` and `_execute_cancel()`.
4. Add defensive handling around `PendingConfirmation.from_dict(...)` for persisted data.
5. If validation fails in handler save-turn logic, treat pending confirmation as missing and log a warning.
6. If validation fails in `confirm_pending_action`, return a Polish error such as `Nie udało się odczytać oczekującej akcji. Utwórz ją ponownie.` and clear the bad pending confirmation if safe.
7. If validation fails in `cancel_pending_action`, clear the bad pending confirmation and return a Polish success/error message saying the invalid pending action was removed.
8. Keep valid pending confirmation behavior unchanged.
9. Add unit tests for invalid pending confirmation data if practical.

## Files To Modify

- `src/weather_agent/adapters/telegram/handler.py`
- `src/weather_agent/llm/tools/rules_tools.py`
- Tests as needed

## Acceptance Criteria

- Malformed persisted pending confirmation cannot crash handler or rules tools.
- `confirm_pending_action` handles invalid pending data with a Polish user-facing error.
- `cancel_pending_action` handles invalid pending data and clears it if possible.
- Valid pending confirmation tests still pass.
- `uv run pytest tests/unit/llm/test_rules_tools.py -x -v` passes.
- `uv run mypy` passes.

title: Keep worker persisted results consistent when one rule failure triggers rollback
description:
## The Problem

In `src/weather_agent/infrastructure/worker/rule_evaluator.py`, when one rule fails, the code calls `await self._session.rollback()` and then continues evaluating other rules.

Problem: earlier successful rules in the same cycle may already have flushed `RuleEvaluationRun` rows. The rollback removes those rows, but `evaluate_rules()` still returns those rules as successful. Returned results and persisted database state can disagree.

## Implementation Steps

1. Read `src/weather_agent/infrastructure/worker/rule_evaluator.py`.
2. Read `tests/unit/infrastructure/worker/test_rule_evaluator.py`.
3. Decide on a simple transaction boundary that keeps returned results and persisted state consistent.
4. Preferred simple fix: commit or use a nested transaction after each successful rule evaluation before moving to the next rule, or isolate each rule in its own transaction boundary.
5. If a rule fails, rollback only that rule's failed DB work, not previous successful rule work.
6. Keep the outer `run_loop()` rollback safety net for exceptions that escape the cycle.
7. Add or update a test where:
   - rule 1 succeeds and creates a `RuleEvaluationRun`
   - rule 2 fails and triggers rollback
   - after `evaluate_rules()`, rule 1's evaluation run is still persisted
8. Keep metrics behavior unchanged unless a test requires otherwise.

## Files To Modify

- `src/weather_agent/infrastructure/worker/rule_evaluator.py`
- `tests/unit/infrastructure/worker/test_rule_evaluator.py`

## Acceptance Criteria

- A later rule failure does not delete DB writes from earlier successful rules in the same cycle.
- Failed rule cleanup still rolls back the session so the next DB access works.
- `uv run pytest tests/unit/infrastructure/worker/test_rule_evaluator.py -x -v` passes.
- `uv run ruff check src/weather_agent/infrastructure/worker/rule_evaluator.py tests/unit/infrastructure/worker/test_rule_evaluator.py` passes.
- `uv run mypy` passes.
close_reason: Implemented and verified with full test suite

title: Instrument LangSmith traces for worker, rule evaluation, and notifications
description:
Problem statement:
Even if the bot conversation path is traced well, the background worker and deterministic notification pipeline will still be a large observability blind spot unless they are instrumented too.

Current behavior from review:
- src/weather_agent/__main__.py configures tracing before bot and worker startup, but there is no explicit tracing around worker lifecycle.
- src/weather_agent/infrastructure/worker/rule_evaluator.py performs evaluation loops, per-rule evaluation, forecast fetching, data preparation, and persistence without explicit LangSmith spans.
- src/weather_agent/adapters/telegram/sender.py sends notifications and logs failures, but there is no explicit LangSmith span around notification send attempts or dry-run sends.
- The project goal is to trace as much as possible; the deterministic worker path is too important to leave untraced.

Goal:
- Make the worker path visible in LangSmith even though it is deterministic and not LLM-driven.
- Capture trace structure for:
  - worker cycle start/end
  - per-rule evaluation
  - forecast refresh before evaluation if enabled
  - evaluation result / notification candidate decision
  - notification send / dry-run send / failure outcome

Implementation guidance for the follow-up agent:
- Add manual LangSmith spans to the worker path using traceable wrappers or equivalent instrumentation.
- Important file touchpoints:
  - src/weather_agent/__main__.py worker startup path
  - src/weather_agent/infrastructure/worker/rule_evaluator.py
  - src/weather_agent/adapters/telegram/sender.py
  - any dedupe / explanation / notification-event logic if that is part of the final send pipeline
- Suggested metadata to consider:
  - rule_id / rule_short_id
  - location_id
  - snapshot_id
  - dry_run
  - notification_candidate
  - chat_id / thread_id for notification sends
- Do not include oversized forecast payloads or secrets in metadata.
- Keep deterministic code deterministic; tracing must observe, not change behavior.

Constraints:
- Runtime rule evaluation must continue to work even if LangSmith is disabled or unavailable.
- Notification failure handling should remain log-friendly and trace-friendly.
design:
Recommended design shape:
- One top-level span per worker cycle.
- Nested spans for each rule evaluation.
- Separate spans for forecast refresh, evaluation-data build, CEL evaluation, and notification send when those steps occur.
- Keep worker traces concise enough to be useful when many rules execute in one cycle.
acceptance_criteria:
This issue is complete when all of the following are true:
- A worker evaluation cycle produces a traceable parent span with child spans for at least one evaluated rule.
- Notification candidate and send paths are visible in traces, including dry-run sends.
- A send failure is visible in the trace/logs without breaking the worker loop.
- Tracing can be disabled without breaking deterministic worker behavior.
notes:
Suggested verification scenario:
- Seed at least one enabled rule and forecast snapshot.
- Run a worker cycle that yields a notification candidate.
- Verify the trace shows worker cycle -> rule evaluation -> notification send (or dry-run send).
close_reason: Implemented and verified with tests, ruff, mypy

title: Simplify conversation orchestration while preserving natural-language UX
description:

Goal:
- Reduce orchestration complexity while preserving:
  - natural-language weather QA
  - natural-language rule authoring
  - reply-based follow-up questions
  - deterministic rule evaluation and provider boundaries

Implementation guidance for the follow-up agent:
- Re-evaluate whether LangGraph is still buying enough value once persisted context is wired correctly.
- Acceptable outcomes include:
  - a smaller, clearer LangGraph with nodes that match real user-turn boundaries, or
  - a simpler explicit dispatcher/state machine in normal Python if that is easier to reason about.
- Do not expand complexity just to preserve LangGraph for its own sake.
- Keep the weather-answering product behavior conversational. The simplification is internal, not a change in user interaction model.
- Likely touchpoints:
  - src/weather_agent/graphs/conversation.py
  - src/weather_agent/graphs/state.py
  - src/weather_agent/graphs/nodes/weather_qa.py
  - src/weather_agent/graphs/nodes/rule_management.py

design:

- Keep deterministic state transitions around confirmation and memory.

title: Harden user-facing error handling and observability boundaries
description:

- Internal logs and observability should retain the technical detail needed for debugging.
- Failure boundaries should be explicit: provider failure, graph failure, rule-generation failure, and Telegram send failure each need sane handling.

  - src/weather_agent/adapters/telegram/commands.py

- Keep observability richer than user-facing responses.

title: Simplify codebase: remove dead code, deduplicate, reduce complexity

6. Test missing-file behavior if practical by monkeypatching `Path.read_text` or the module path calculation. Do not rename the real `AGENTS.md` file.
7. Keep `_load_agents_md()` behavior simple. If the current implementation is already good, only add tests.
